newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC says parent sales in 96/97 exceeded 4 trln yen.
newsitem.headline: NEC says parent sales in 96/97 exceeded 4 trln yen.

text.p: NEC Corp president Hisashi Kaneko said on Friday that the company's parent sales in fiscal 1996/97 exceeded four trillion yen.
Kaneko said the company would invest 15 billion yen in 1997/98, which began on April 1, to build new production facilities for 64 megabit dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips.
The new facilities will be able to produce chips with circuit lines as fine as 0.25 micron wide, he said.
NEC's current 64 megabit DRAM plant uses 0.35 micron technology.
He also said the company planned investments totalling 400 billion yen over the next three years worldwide for chip plants using etching technology finer than 0.25 micron.
The investments will boost the company's production capacity of the advanced chips by 200,000 eight-inch wafers per month, he said.
Kaneko also said NEC expects to post 1.10 trillion yen in sales from its semiconductor business in 1996/97 and predicted that the figure would increase to 1.21 trillion yen in 1997/98.
NEC on Friday opened a new plant in Hiroshima for making DRAM chips with 0.35 micron-wide circuit lines. Total investment in the plant was about 70 billion yen.
The new plant has a production capacity of 20,000 wafers per month.
Kaneko, in Hiroshima to attend the opening ceremony of the plant, said the company expects to see sales and profits increase in the current 1997/98 business year despite some uncertainties.
He said parent current profit for 1996/97 is likely to have considerably exceeded the initially forecast figure of 105 billion yen.
He also said NEC had originally expected to post parent sales of 3.95 trillion yen for 1996/97.
